data_policy: Yahoo historical daily closes were retrieved in one later snapshot. Frozen-v1 features and states use only observations dated <= t, but past Yahoo vintages are NOT available. These are date-ordered retrospective OOS research replays, NOT historical live predictions or deployable probabilities.

design.calibration_gate: For every destination: >=50 positives, every populated one-of-five fixed-width score bins >=30 observations, ECE <=0.05 and max bin gap <=0.10.
design.embargo: last training target index < first test origin index - horizon
design.hidden_model: NOT RUN: without historical source vintages, a latent switching model's state identifiability and fair point-in-time comparison cannot be established. No likelihood-based selection or hyperparameter search.
design.improvement_gate: Log loss AND multiclass Brier >=1% better than BOTH persistence and state-conditional Markov on identical rows; dual-metric wins in >=2/3 of annual blocks and positive gains in all three chronological thirds.
design.logistic: 3-class, fixed L2=10, train-only scaling; DE-RISK reference
design.markov: direct empirical h-step conditional frequencies from training labels only
design.persistence: one-hot current regime; scoring-only floor 1e-6 for log loss
design.protocol_status: Rules are fixed in this implementation for reproducible replay, but no independently dated preregistration exists. Treat findings as exploratory.
design.provenance_gate: archived, dated Yahoo vintages available BEFORE each forecast origin
design.sample_gate: >=1500 common OOS origins, >=6 test blocks, >=50 distinct one-step entries per destination
design.training: expanding, initial 1260 canonical sessions; tests in 252-session blocks

1.recommendation_reason: Historical Yahoo source vintages were not captured at each session: real-time point-in-time availability cannot be certified. Quantitative gates alone cannot override the provenance gate.

3.recommendation_reason: Historical Yahoo source vintages were not captured at each session: real-time point-in-time availability cannot be certified. Quantitative logistic gates also fail.
